record.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
record.original_question: If there is a non-trivial satisfiability algorithm for Boolean circuits of size cn on n inputs, does that imply cn lower bounds for Boolean-circuit complexity?

evidence.quote: Do non-trivial satisfiability algorithms for circuits of size cn imply cn lower bounds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Boolean circuit (over the standard De Morgan basis with AND, OR, NOT gates of fan-in at most 2) on n input bits is said to have size s if it consists of at most s gates. Fix a constant c > 0. A "non-trivial satisfiability algorithm" for the class of Boolean circuits of size cn on n inputs is a deterministic algorithm that, given as input a description of such a circuit C, decides whether there exists x ∈ {0,1}^n with C(x) = 1, in worst-case time 2^n / s(n) for some superpolynomial (or otherwise non-trivial) function s(n) → ∞ — that is, an algorithm that beats exhaustive search by a non-trivial factor on this circuit class.

Question: Does the existence, for every constant c > 0, of a non-trivial satisfiability algorithm for Boolean circuits of size cn on n inputs imply that there is a language in some "natural" complexity class (e.g., E^{NP}, NEXP, or similar) that, for every constant c > 0, requires Boolean circuits of size at least cn (i.e., linear lower bounds with arbitrarily large constant)?

Equivalently: prove or refute the implication

   "for every c, a non-trivial SAT algorithm exists for size-cn circuits"  ⟹  "for every c, there is an explicit function requiring circuits of size cn".
artifact.category_tag: Boolean circuit lower bounds and SAT algorithms
artifact.status_search_result: The connection between non-trivial circuit-SAT algorithms and circuit lower bounds (Williams' program) is known to yield NEXP ⊄ P/poly-style consequences from non-trivial SAT for polynomial-size circuits, and analogous results for restricted classes. However, the specific question of whether non-trivial SAT for linear-size (size cn) circuits implies linear (cn) circuit lower bounds for general unrestricted circuits remains an open problem in the area, as of recent surveys on unrestricted Boolean circuit lower bounds.

status_evidence.title: Complexity Lower Bounds from Algorithm Design — R. Ryan Williams
status_evidence.snippet: Even slightly nontrivial algorithms could imply Boolean circuit lower bounds; non-trivial circuit-SAT for poly-size circuits implies NEXP ⊄ P/poly.
status_evidence.claim: The SAT-to-lower-bounds program is active and established for poly-size circuits, with linear-size analogues remaining open.

status_evidence.title: New Algorithms for QBF Satisfiability and Implications for Circuit Complexity (ECCC TR13-108)
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements over brute force for QBF-SAT would imply breakthroughs in circuit complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Non-trivial SAT algorithms continue to be studied as a route to circuit lower bounds, but the linear-size case is not resolved.
